title: Print styles and print-friendly document structure
learningObjectives: Explain print styles and print-friendly document structure and apply accurate document metadata or print structure.

understand.concept: Print-friendly HTML uses semantic structure and print media styles to hide unnecessary controls, adjust colours, avoid awkward page breaks, and preserve readable links and tables. The print stylesheet should not remove information needed to understand the document.
understand.whyItMatters: A screen-only layout may waste paper or print navigation and buttons. Print styles should preserve the actual content and be checked using print preview or a real PDF/print output.
understand.analogy: A print stylesheet prepares a clean reading copy of the same document rather than creating a separate, incomplete version.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; browser metadata and search/social platform processing are governed by their respective specifications and policies.

explain.narrative: Navigation and the button are hidden for print while the report content remains. Verify the result in print preview.

questions.prompt: Which media query targets printed output?
questions.explanation: The print media query applies styles in print and print-preview contexts.

questions.prompt: What is the most important rule for page metadata?
options: It must accurately describe the actual page
It should contain as many keywords as possible
It can claim features not present on the page
questions.answer: It must accurately describe the actual page
questions.explanation: Metadata should be accurate, consistent, and not misleading.
